belief: I have to hide my difference to be accepted.
origins: A birthmark, scar, limb difference, stutter, or other visible or hidden difference can lead to covering up, avoiding photos, or staying out of view. The effort is exhausting and can reinforce shame.
teaches: “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?” God is not embarrassed by how He made you. “The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor.” Real acceptance does not require hiding. Choose to share at your own pace with safe people.
self_statements: If they see it, they will reject me.
errors: Believing I am either hidden and accepted or exposed and rejected.
Feeling shame and concluding I must hide.
questions: What do I hide, and what does hiding cost me?
Who has seen it and still accepted me?
What does God say about how He made me?
What if I shared with one safe person?
What response would I like to practice if someone asks?
What parts of my difference are also a strength?
truth: God made me as I am, and He is not ashamed of me. I can share at my own pace with safe people, and I do not need to hide to be loved.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I do not need to hide.
I choose how and when to share.
log: Each week, note one small step toward openness.
prayer: Creator, You made me as I am. Free me from shame, and give me safe people and courage to be open at my own pace. Amen.
